fullPassage: Ancient Athens was home to the first democracy, and it produced some great thinkers. As democracy started to fail, the philosophers of the time tried to figure out why and to think of ways to fix it. One of these philosophers was Plato(427-347 B.C.), a student of Socrates(469-399 B.C.). Plato began to doubt the democracy of his time and tried to think of a better option. In one of his most famous works, The Republic, Plato proposed his ideal society. It was based on what he saw as the four virtues of the state: wisdom, courage, self-discipline, and justice. He designated a different class of people to fulfill three of these virtues. The wise would rule as “philosopher kings,” the brave would act as “guardians,” the self-disciplined would do “manual work,” and the whole of society would work together toward justice. Plato saw people as being naturally inclined to serve one of these roles because of their soul. The soul, according to Plato, is divided into three parts: the rational, the will, and the appetite. If the individual is governed more by the rational element, he or she is suited to rule. Someone who is governed by the will would make a good guardian, and a person governed by the appetite would make a good worker. The ultimate goals of society, for Plato, were fulfillment of needs and happiness. Everyone has needs, and everyone has abilities. But people don’t have the range of abilities required to meet all of their individual needs. Therefore, he felt, society must work together to satisfy the needs of all people. When everyone specializes in their occupation and then exchanges the fruits of their labor with others, all people can meet their needs and be happy. Crucially, Plato believed that the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers or philosophers were made kings, as it is the wisdom of their decision-making that is the key to the success of a social unit. Plato’s Republic was designed to put in place a system that addressed the innate characteristics of the people. Although its aim seems too impractical to become reality, his thoughts laid the foundations of Western philosophy.

det.korean: a barrier to the growth=성장의 장벽 / an obstacle to the unity=통합의 장애물 / the key to the success=성공의 열쇠 / a threat to the stability=안정의 위협

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

① 민주주의가 '실패하기' 시작한 시기라 '번성'은 반대예요

③ 사람들은 모든 필요를 혼자 충족할 '능력의 범위'가 없다고 했어요

④ 그 목표는 너무 비현실적이어서 현실이 되기 어렵다고 했어요
det.tip: 지배 요소(이성/의지/욕구) → 역할(통치/수호/노동).

ch: 플라톤은 영혼의 어느 요소에 더 지배되는지에 따라 사람의 역할이 정해진다고 보았다.
플라톤은 누구나 혼자서 자신의 모든 필요를 충족할 수 있다고 보았다.
플라톤의 이상 사회는 현실에서 완벽하게 실현되었다.

questions.passage: Ancient Athens was home to the first democracy, and it produced some great thinkers. As democracy started to fail, the philosophers of the time tried to figure out why and to think of ways to fix it. One of these philosophers was Plato(427-347 B.C.), a student of Socrates(469-399 B.C.). Plato began to doubt the democracy of his time and tried to think of a better option. In one of his most famous works, The Republic, Plato proposed his ideal society. It was based on what he saw as the four virtues of the state: wisdom, courage, self-discipline, and justice. He designated a different class of people to fulfill three of these virtues. The wise would rule as “philosopher kings,” the brave would act as “guardians,” the self-disciplined would do “manual work,” and the whole of society would work together toward justice. Plato saw people as being naturally inclined to serve one of these roles because of their soul. The soul, according to Plato, is divided into three parts: the rational, the will, and the appetite. If the individual is governed more by the rational element, he or she is suited to rule. Someone who is governed by the will would make a good guardian, and a person governed by the appetite would make a good worker. The ultimate goals of society, for Plato, were fulfillment of needs and happiness. Everyone has needs, and everyone has abilities. But people don’t have the range of abilities required to meet all of their individual needs. Therefore, he felt, society must work together to satisfy the needs of all people. When everyone specializes in their occupation and then exchanges the fruits of their labor with others, all people can meet their needs and be happy. Crucially, Plato believed that the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers or philosophers were made kings, as it is the wisdom of their decision-making that is the key to the success of a social unit. Plato’s Republic was designed to put in place a system that addressed the innate characteristics of the people. Although its aim seems too impractical to become reality, his thoughts laid the foundations of Western philosophy.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 욕구에 지배되는 사람은 '노동자'에 적합하다고 했으므로, 통치자로 가장 적합하다는 것은 사실과 반대예요.
det.analysis:
④ 본문에서 욕구(appetite)에 지배되는 사람은 '좋은 노동자(a good worker)'가 되고, 통치에 적합한 것은 '이성'에 지배되는 사람이라고 했어요. 따라서 불일치예요 ←정답

① 'wisdom, courage, self-discipline, and justice'와 일치해요

② 'specializes ... exchanges the fruits of their labor ... meet their needs'와 일치해요

③ 'kings became philosophers or philosophers were made kings'와 일치해요
det.tip: appetite → good worker (통치는 rational의 몫).

ch: 국가의 네 가지 덕목은 지혜, 용기, 절제, 정의이다.
사람들은 전문화와 노동의 결실 교환을 통해 서로의 필요를 충족한다.
플라톤은 왕이 철학자가 되거나 철학자가 왕이 될 때 완전한 사회가 가능하다고 보았다.
플라톤은 욕구에 지배되는 사람이 통치자로 가장 적합하다고 보았다.

det.korean: 사람들은 혼자서 모든 필요를 채울 만큼의 능력을 갖추지 못했기에 사회가 함께 협력해야 한다고 했어요.

① 본문 'people don't have the range of abilities required to meet all of their individual needs ... society must work together'와 일치해요 ←정답

ch: 사람들은 혼자서 모든 필요를 충족할 만큼 다양한 능력을 갖추지 못했기에 사회가 협력해야 한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글은 영혼의 본성(이성·의지·욕구)에 따라 역할을 나누어 모두의 필요를 충족하려 한 플라톤의 이상 국가론을 다뤄요.
det.analysis:
③ 네 덕목·세 계층·세 부분의 영혼·전문화와 협력 등 '영혼의 본성에 기초한 역할 분담'이라는 플라톤 이상 국가론을 다루므로 주제로 알맞아요 ←정답

② 민주주의와 군주제 비교가 주제가 아니에요

④ 분업의 경제적 효과를 논한 글이 아니에요

ch: 고대 아테네에서 철학이 쇠퇴하게 된 과정
영혼의 본성에 기초하여 각자의 역할을 나눈 플라톤의 이상 국가론

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the fruits of their labor가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 (영어로) 쓰시오.

플라톤은 그 민주주의를 의심하기 시작했다

questions.passage: Plato saw people as being naturally inclined to serve one of these roles because of their soul. The soul, according to Plato, is __________ (divide) into three parts: the rational, the will, and the appetite.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: divide → divided: 'is ______ into' be동사 뒤 수동태라 과거분사 divided로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'The soul ... is __________ into three parts'에서 빈칸은 be동사(is) 뒤예요. 영혼이 세 부분으로 '나뉘는' 것이니 수동태(be + 과거분사)가 필요해요. 그래서 동사 divide를 과거분사 divided로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 divide를 divided로 써요.
det.tip: is divided into ~ = ~로 나뉘다 (수동태).

questions.passage: Ancient Athens was home to the first democracy, and it produced some great thinkers. As democracy started to fail, the philosophers of the time tried to figure out why and to think of ways to fix it. One of these philosophers was Plato(427-347 B.C.), a student of Socrates(469-399 B.C.). Plato began to doubt the democracy of his time and tried to think of a better option. In one of his most famous works, The Republic, Plato proposed his ideal society. It was based on what he saw as the four virtues of the state: wisdom, courage, self-discipline, and justice. He designated a different class of people to fulfill three of these virtues. The wise would rule as “philosopher kings,” the brave would act as “guardians,” the self-disciplined would do “manual work,” and the whole of society would work together toward justice. Plato saw people as being naturally inclined to serve one of these roles because of their soul. The soul, according to Plato, is divided into three parts: the rational, the will, and the appetite. If the individual is governed more by the rational element, he or she is suited to rule. Someone who is governed by the will would make a good guardian, and a person governed by the appetite would make a good worker. The ultimate goals of society, for Plato, were fulfillment of needs and happiness. Everyone has needs, and everyone has abilities. But people don’t have the range of abilities required to meet all of their individual needs. Therefore, he felt, society must work together to satisfy the needs of all people. When everyone specializes in their occupation and then exchanges the fruits of their labor with others, all people can meet their needs and be happy. Crucially, Plato believed that __________ or philosophers were made kings, as it is the wisdom of their decision-making that is the key to the success of a social unit. Plato’s Republic was designed to put in place a system that addressed the innate characteristics of the people. Although its aim seems too impractical to become reality, his thoughts laid the foundations of Western philosophy.

완전한 사회는 왕이 철학자가 될 때에만 이루어질 것이다
[조건] (1) became, kings, occur, only, perfect, philosophers, society, the, when, would 를 모두 사용 (2) 10단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '완전한 사회는 왕이 철학자가 될 때에만 이루어질 것이다'를 the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers로 영작해요.
det.analysis:
주어는 the perfect society(완전한 사회)예요.

→ 동사는 would occur(이루어질 것이다)를 써요.

→ '~할 때에만'은 'only when ~'으로 연결해요.

→ when절은 '왕이 철학자가 되다'라서 kings became philosophers로 써요.

→ 완성: the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers
det.tip: only when + 주어 + 동사 = ~할 때에만.

questions.wa: the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers
accept: the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers

[ aim / become / impractical / its / reality / seems / to / too ] (8단어)

det.korean: '그 목표는 너무 비현실적이어서 현실이 되기 어려워 보인다'를 its aim seems too impractical to become reality로 배열해요.
